page.layout: One printed page of text, framed by an ornamental border; running head at top; no marginal notes in the text block. Right of the page edge is show-through from the facing page and is left out.

main_text.p: Augurell[?] imperio Romano Diocletianû ex arte illa metuisse, an Sybillinis monitis nec ne, parum compertum habemus. Licet autem quo ad chymiam in specie de Mose nihil constet, tamen æneum serpentem jussu Dei fecit & fudit Moses: aureum vero vitulum jussu Dei combussit & contrivit, usq; adeò, ut inspersum aquæ, populo bibendum propinârit, Exod.23. Quod an ulli uspiam aurifices hodie præstare possint, ut aurû comburendo simpliciter fiat potabile, ipsi viderint. Jam vero Reges Christûm adorantes, & Aurum, thus, Myrrham, Regiq; hominiq; Deoq;, offerentes, non frustra Magos, nempè naturales, donorumq; suorum scientes & gnaros fuisse constat: sicut & Arabes hac ipsa

page.notes: Printed text is partly damaged and set in a worn type; the word after "Augurell" is uncertain and marked [?]. The catchword "ipsa" is set at the lower right of the text block. A faint offset from the facing page's text appears under the lines "Aurum"/"hac ipsa" and is not transcribed.
